questions.q: What is a Power BI app?
options: A read-only, packaged distribution of a workspace's dashboards, reports, and semantic models
A separate editable copy of a workspace that consumers can modify
A mobile-only version of Power BI with no desktop equivalent
A tenant setting that enables external sharing
questions.explain: An app packages content from a workspace for read-only consumption by a broader audience — only the workspace's own Admins/Members can edit the underlying content.

questions.q: Does publishing an app automatically expose everything in its source workspace?
options: No — only items explicitly added via the Content tab's 'Add content' are included
Yes — all workspace content becomes visible in the app automatically
Only dashboards are included automatically; reports must be added manually
Apps have no concept of 'content' separate from the workspace
questions.explain: The Content tab's Add content step is how specific items get pulled into the app — publishing doesn't automatically expose everything in the underlying workspace.

questions.q: What is an app 'audience' used for?
options: Letting different groups of people see a different slice of content from the same underlying app
Setting the app's color theme and logo
Determining which workspace the app is published from
Scheduling when the app refreshes its data
questions.explain: Up to 25 audience groups can be created per app, each with independent show/hide toggles per item, so different people see different content from the same app.

questions.q: If an item is hidden from every audience in an app, is the underlying data fully protected?
options: Not necessarily — if 'Allow access to hidden content' is enabled, a direct link can still reach it, and RLS/OLS are the only real data-level protection
Yes — hiding an item from an audience is equivalent to removing it from the semantic model
Yes, hiding always blocks direct links regardless of other settings
Hidden items are automatically deleted from the app after 30 days
questions.explain: Hiding is a navigation convenience, not a security control. A direct link can still reach hidden content if 'Allow access to hidden content' is on, and the app's real data security comes entirely from RLS/OLS on the underlying semantic model.

questions.q: What happens to newly added workspace content the first time you update an already-published app?
options: It's marked hidden by default for every audience, and must be manually unhidden
It's automatically shown to every audience immediately
It's automatically shown only to the 'entire organization' audience
Updating an app is not possible once it's published — a new app must be created
questions.explain: By default, newly added content to an already-published app is marked invisible for every audience group — you must go into each audience and manually unhide it.
